Subject: High latency + 504s on inference calls since 08:45 PST — urgent

Hi Priya,

We're seeing a big regression on our inference traffic to Redwood starting ~08:45 PST — p50/p95 latency jumped 4-5x and about 8% of requests are returning 504/502. This is hitting our checkout path and hitting business metrics (cart abandonment up).

Attached: orchidlane_latency_trace.pcap and a short tail of application logs (orchidlane_inference_logs_07-14.txt). From our side the failed requests appear to timeout waiting on a remote HTTP 502/504; we also observed intermittent DNS lookup timeouts to inference.redwood.net.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood side (peering, proxy, firewall rules) or if this looks like a peering/DNS issue from your infra? We need an ETA and mitigation steps — our legal/procurement team is already on the thread due to impact.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform
OrchidLane

Hi Elena — thanks for the report and the captures. We're pulling the initial telemetry now. I've looped in ops (Marissa, Jonas) and infra (Rishi) for immediate triage.

Quick notes / ask:
- We haven't rolled a config change this morning on hosted routing, but we are seeing elevated NAT conntrack and proxy queueing in the us-west cluster (monitoring alert fired at 08:40).
- Can you confirm whether OrchidLane recently changed any VPC-peering routes or egress NAT IPs? Also, do you have private DNS/NAT changes to share?

Immediate plan (1) we will snapshot routing and dnat tables and search for asymmetric pathing in the traces; (2) if we confirm a peering/DNS handoff, we will push a temporary route override to route OrchidLane traffic to the nearest dedicated edge (fallback) to avoid the overloaded proxy; (3) coordinate an exec sync if mitigation requires a brief re-IP.

I'll send an internal status update in 20 minutes and a recommended mitigation after Jonas completes the path audit.

-Priya

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 504s on inference calls since 08:45 PST — urgent

Triage summary (first pass):
- Correlated OrchidLane source IPs to peering session us-west-2-a. At 08:39 we see a spike in TCP retransmits and SYN timeouts toward our proxy fleet, and simultaneous increase in DNS response latency from the resolver cluster servicing that peering.
- Path evidence suggests an intermittent BGP micro-flap on the peering fabric plus a delayed DNS cache eviction causing requests to take a circuitous egress (extra hop through shared transit proxy). The extra hop is causing queueing and connection tails -> 504s.
- NAT conntrack exhaustion observed on a subset of puma-proxy nodes (max conntrack ~96% on 2 hosts). Those nodes are overloaded and returning 502s under queue pressure.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:40):
1) Drained two overloaded proxy instances and shifted traffic to healthy nodes (reduced error rate from ~8% to ~4% observed at 09:48).
2) Pushed a temporary route-policy to prefer direct peering path for OrchidLane prefix (observed p95 latency improve ~30% on the direct path).
3) Increased DNS cache TTL for our internal resolver to avoid repeated upstream lookups while we stabilize peering.

Remaining actions:
- Validate with OrchidLane whether they rolled a peering/BGP change at 08:30–08:45.
- Run conntrack garbage-collection and increase conntrack limit on puma-proxy pool if traffic surge persists.

I've attached the path-trace snippet and conntrack dump. If Orchidlane can confirm no config changes, we will open peering fabric escalation with the cloud provider and coordinate an executive briefing.

Jonas Weber
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Orchidlane incident brief + exec ask (follow-up)

Folks — final incident brief and ask for executive support. Summary below for leadership.

What happened:
- 2026-07-14 08:39–09:16 PST: OrchidLane experienced elevated inference latencies and ~8% 504/502 errors driven by a combination of (a) transient BGP micro-flap on the us-west peering fabric, (b) DNS resolver latency causing additional egress hops, and (c) conntrack pressure on 2 proxy nodes.
- Impact: checkout failures and revenue impact for OrchidLane (customer reports ~35 minutes of elevated errors).

What we did:
- Drained and replaced affected proxy instances; increased DNS TTL and applied a temporary route-policy to prefer direct peering path (restored nominal performance by ~09:50).
- Opened support ticket with our cloud provider (ticket #CP-98723) to investigate fabric instability and BGP flap root cause.
- Coordinated with Orchidlane; customer confirmed no local peering/DNS change. They will provide additional flow captures on request.

Risk/ask:
- We need executive visibility for two items: (1) expedite cloud provider investigation (we may need a fabric configuration change or soft re-home of the session), and (2) customer remediation (commercial credit request from Procurement). OrchidLane has asked for an exec sync if we require IP/re-route changes that affect their security posture.

Suggested next steps:
1) Markus: please approve immediate exec outreach to cloud provider account team to push CP-98723 to priority P1.
2) Marissa/Rishi: prepare proposed customer remediation (one-time credit + postmortem) and a timeline for a permanent mitigation (conntrack tuning + routing policy hardening).
3) Jonas: schedule postmortem and include traceroute/DNS correlation; coordinate a joint test window with OrchardLane to validate stable peering.

I've attached the final diagnostic dump and our proposed customer-facing postmortem. I'll schedule a 30m exec call pending Markus' approval.

-Priya Natarajan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
